# Title:Generalized Images for Brownian First Passage to Monomial Boundaries
> Abstract:We study the first passage of Brownian motion to a monomial moving boundary. For every integer degree at least two, we construct a time-independent signed image measure whose heat potential is the killed Brownian transition density on a nonzero interval of the natural Brownian time scale. The image density is determined by a second-kind Volterra equation in the image coordinate, not by the classical Volterra equations in time for the hitting density. Its kernel is an explicit Wright function, and the first-passage density is recovered afterwards from the boundary flux.

### Abstract

We study the first passage of Brownian motion to a monomial moving boundary. For every integer degree at least two, we construct a time-independent signed image measure whose heat potential is the killed Brownian transition density on a nonzero interval of the natural Brownian time scale. The image density is determined by a second-kind Volterra equation in the image coordinate, not by the classical Volterra equations in time for the hitting density. We propose a new method to obtain the boundary crossing probabilities or the first passage time distribution for linear and nonlinear boundaries for Brownian motion. ###### Abstract

We study the first passage of Brownian motion to a monomial moving boundary. For every integer degree at least two, we construct a time-independent signed image measure whose heat potential is the killed Brownian transition density on a nonzero interval of the natural Brownian time scale. The image density is determined by a second-kind Volterra equation in the image coordinate, not by the classical Volterra equations in time for the hitting density. Its kernel is an explicit Wright function, and the first-passage density is recovered afterwards from the boundary flux. Exponential bounds establish convergence, while a beta-moment transform connects the Wright kernel with the finite-order differential hierarchy previously obtained from transported moving zeros. A cubic numerical experiment independently checks the resulting density against simulated Brownian paths.

octen.title: First Passage Density of Brownian Motion with Two-sided Piecewise Linear Boundaries | Acta Mathematica Sinica, English Series | Springer Nature Link
octen.snippet:
Abstract
The first passage time has many applications in fields like finance, econometrics, statistics, and biology. However, explicit formulas for the first passage density have only been obtained for a few cases. This paper derives an explicit formula for the first passage density of Brownian motion with two-sided piecewise continuous boundaries which may have some points of discontinuity. Approximations are used to obtain a simplified formula for estimating the first passage density. Moreover, the results are also generalized to the case of two-sided general nonlinear boundaries. Simulations can be easily carried out with Monte Carlo method and it is demonstrated for several typical two-sided boundaries that the proposed approximation method offers a highly accurate approximation of first passage density.

octen.title: First-passage times of two-dimensional Brownian motion | Advances in Applied Probability | Cambridge Core
octen.snippet:
Published online by Cambridge University Press: 11 January 2017
First-passage times (FPTs) of two-dimensional Brownian motion have many applications in quantitative finance. However, despite various attempts since the 1960s, there are few analytical solutions available. By solving a nonhomogeneous modified Helmholtz equation in an infinite wedge, we find analytical solutions for the Laplace transforms of FPTs; these Laplace transforms can be inverted numerically. The FPT problems lead to a class of bivariate exponential distributions which are absolute continuous but do not have the memoryless property. We also prove that the density of the absolute difference of FPTs tends to ∞ if and only if the correlation between the two Brownian motions is positive.

octen.title: [2306.17656v2] First-passage time of a Brownian motion: two unexpected journeys
octen.snippet:
Condensed Matter > Statistical Mechanics
  [Submitted on 30 Jun 2023 (v1), revised 7 Jul 2023 (this version, v2), latest version 8 Jul 2024 (v3)]
    Title:First-passage time of a Brownian motion: two unexpected journeys
View PDF HTML (experimental)Abstract:The distribution of the first-passage time T_a for a Brownian particle with drift \mu subject to hitting an absorber at a level a>0 is well-known and given by its density \gamma(t) = \frac{a}{\sqrt{2 \pi t^3} } e^{-\frac{(a-\mu t)^2}{2 t}}, t>0, which is normalized only if \mu \geq 0. In this article, we show that there are two other families of diffusion processes (the first with one parameter and the second with two parameters) having the same first passage-time distribution when \mu <0. In both cases we establish the propagators and study in detail these new processes. An immediate consequence is that the distribution of the first-passage time does not allow us to know if the process comes from a drifted Brownian motion or from one of these new processes.

Title: Taylor expansions for first-passage time distributions of Brownian motion with moving boundaries

Authors: Vincent Liang
View PDF HTML (experimental)
Abstract: We analyse the distribution of the first-passage time of Brownian motion to a time-dependent boundary as a function of the boundary. We prove that the boundary-to-distribution map is infinitely many times differentiable along the Cameron-Martin space $\mathscr{H},$ and obtain a with a bound on the truncation error Taylor expansion with a bound on the truncation error. We obtain identities connecting (i) the $\mathscr{H}$-derivatives of the first-passage time distribution, (ii) the Wiener-Itô chaos kernels of the indicator that the Brownian motion stays below the boundary, and (iii) Krylov-Veretennikov-Zvonkin-type operators. These identities yield relatively tractable representations for the $\mathscr{H}$-derivatives of the first-passage time distribution when the taboo transition density is available, notably for linear boundaries. As an application of the above results we propose Taylor approximations up to second order of the first-passage time distribution. In the examples considered, the first-order approximation is more accurate than the classical tangent approximation and its hazard-rate variant, while remaining straightforward to implement.

First Passage Time for Brownian Motion and Piecewise Linear Boundaries

Zhiyong Jin 1 · Liqun Wang 1,2
Received: 24 June 2015 / Accepted: 27 November 2015 / Published online: 9 December 2015 © Springer Science+Business Media New York 2015
Abstract We propose a new approach to calculating the first passage time densities for Brownian motion crossing piecewise linear boundaries which can be discontinuous. Using this approach we obtain explicit formulas for the first passage densities and show that they are continuously differentiable except at the break points of the boundaries. Further- more, these formulas can be used to approximate the first passage time distributions for general nonlinear boundaries.

...

The main stream approaches are based on certain differential or integral equations and deal with smooth boundaries only. We proposed an approach that apply to smooth as well as discontinuous boundaries. Using this approach we have derived explicit formulas for the piecewise linear boundary crossing probability and density for Brownian motion. The derived formulas can be used to approximate the BCP or FPD for more general nonlinear boundaries. We have demonstrated that the numerical calculation can be easily done by Monte Carlo simulation method and the simulation error can be easily assessed. We have tested our method on some well-known benchmark examples and our numerical results show that this method produces fairly good approximations. We have also shown how to obtain closed-form BCP or FPD for a class of diffusion processes that can be expressed as piecewise monotone functionals of Brownian motion, including geometric Brownian motion, O-U processes and growth processes.

parallel.title: The first-passage time of the Brownian motion to a curved boundary: an algorithmic approach
parallel.snippet:
###### Abstract

Under some weak conditions, the first-passage time of the Brownian motion to a continuous curved
boundary is an almost surely finite stopping time. Its probability density function (pdf) is explicitly known only in few particular cases.
Several mathematical studies proposed to approximate the pdf in a quite general framework or even to simulate
this hitting time using a discrete time approximation of the Brownian motion. The authors study a new algorithm
which permits to simulate the first-passage time using an iterating procedure. The convergence rate presented in
this paper suggests that the method is very efficient.

Key words and phrases: first-passage time, Brownian motion, potential theory, randomized algorithm.

#### Approximation of the probability density function

For particular cases, the probability density function of the Brownian passage time can be computed explicitly. Lerche  [30 ] used the method of images in order to obtain explicit expressions of the p.d.f. $p$ defined by $p(t)\,dt=\mathbb{P}(\tau_{\varphi}\in dt)$ . However only few cases are concerned by such a study.

Durbin  [12 , 13 ] proposed to approximate the first-passage distribution $p(t)$ of the Brownian motion as follows: $p$ can be represented by an expansion

| |$p(t)=\sum_{j=1}^{k}(-1)^{j-1}q_{j}(t)+(-1)^{k}r_{k}(t),\quad k\geq 1,$ | |

where $q_{j}$ for $1\leq j\leq k$ and $r_{k}$ are defined by multiple integrals depending on the boundary $\varphi$ . The approximation simply consists in truncating the expansion.
Let us note that the first term corresponds in fact to the tangent approximation of Strassen  [38 ] and Daniels  [9 ] , see also  [16 ] .

The distribution of the first-passage time (FPT) $T_{a}$ for a Brownian particle with drift $\mu$ subject to hitting an absorber at a level $a>0$ is well-known and given by its density $\gamma(t)=\frac{a}{\sqrt{2\pi t^{3}}}e^{-\frac{(a-\mu t)^{2}}{2t}},t>0$ , which is normalized only if $\mu\geq 0$ . A one-dimensional diffusion used in finance almost always lives on a half-line: an interest rate on (0, ∞), a variance on (0, ∞), a stock price on (0, ∞). At the edge you want two yes-or-no answers. A barrier option dies when the underlying leaves a corridor. A firm defaults when its asset value leaves the solvent region. A fund pays a management fee every day until it is wound up. ultimate.title: Generalized Images for Brownian First Passage to Monomial Boundaries
ultimate.snippet: We study the first passage of Brownian motion to a monomial moving boundary. For every integer degree at least two, we construct a time-independent signed image measure whose heat potential is the killed Brownian transition density on a nonzero interval of the natural Brownian time scale. The image density is determined by a second-kind Volterra equation in the image coordinate, not by the classical Volterra equations in time for the hitting density. Its kernel is an explicit Wright function, and the first-passage density is recovered afterwards from the boundary flux. Exponential bounds establish convergence, while a beta-moment transform connects the Wright kernel with the finite-order differential hierarchy previously obtained from transported moving zeros. A cubic numerical experiment independently checks the resulting density against simulated Brownian paths.

ultimate.snippet: We analyse the distribution of the first-passage time of Brownian motion to a time-dependent boundary as a function of the boundary. We prove that the boundary-to-distribution map is infinitely many times differentiable along the Cameron-Martin space $\mathscr{H},$ and obtain a with a bound on the truncation error Taylor expansion with a bound on the truncation error. We obtain identities connecting (i) the $\mathscr{H}$-derivatives of the first-passage time distribution, (ii) the Wiener-Itô chaos kernels of the indicator that the Brownian motion stays below the boundary, and (iii) Krylov-Veretennikov-Zvonkin-type operators. As an application of the above results we propose Taylor approximations up to second order of the first-passage time distribution. In the examples considered, the first-order approximation is more accurate than the classical tangent approximation and its hazard-rate variant, while remaining straightforward to implement.
